route: The handicap-zero class $\mathcal R$ against its own tangent cut: I did not get a family that defeats M7, and the reason turned out to be a theorem in the opposite direction. I attached to $\mathcal R$ a new object, the visit number $\kappa(G)$ of the harmonic normal form, proved that the handicap controls it ($B\succeq\lambda I\Rightarrow\kappa\le3|C|/\lambda$), proved that bounded $\kappa$ is a polynomial class by a certified reduced value iteration, and so settled deliverable (B) and the question of rem:handicap-base on the strongly convex slice negatively. Deliverable (C) is refuted with two built games; deliverable (A) is not achieved, but (D) yielded an algebraic normal form for the cut and the first quantitative bound on what one cut buys, plus a game on which M7 is silent for two rounds.
object: The visit number $\kappa(G):=\max_{\alpha\in\{0,1\}^{C}}\|(I-Q_\alpha)^{-1}\|_\infty$ of the harmonic normal form over $C$ --- the largest expected number of visits to the controlled set under a positional pair, where $Q_\alpha$ is the first-passage matrix of the selection $\alpha$ --- together with the spectral inequality that ties it to the handicap matrix $B=\mathrm{sym}(R_0^{\mathsf T}R_1)$ of rem:handicap-base.
headline: If the handicap matrix of a stopping SSG satisfies $B\succeq\lambda I$ then every positional pair visits the controlled vertices at most $3|C|/\lambda$ times in expectation, and the strongly convex slice $\mathcal R_\lambda$ with $\lambda\ge1/\mathrm{poly}(N)$ is therefore a polynomial class.

results.name: ht:lem-sigmin --- the handicap bounds every selection from below
results.statement: Let G be a stopping SSG with |C| = k >= 1, let P_0,P_1 be the first-passage matrices of the harmonic normal form over C, and let B = sym(R_0^T R_1) satisfy B >= lambda I with lambda > 0. Then for EVERY selection alpha in {0,1}^C and every d in R^C, ||(I-Q_alpha)d||_2 >= (lambda/(3 sqrt k))||d||_2, where Q_alpha is the matrix whose v-th row is P_{alpha(v)}(v,.). Hence ||(I-Q_alpha)^{-1}||_2 <= 3 sqrt k/lambda, ||(I-Q_alpha)^{-1}||_inf <= 3k/lambda, and kappa(G) <= 3|C|/lambda.
results.why_not_implied: rem:handicap-base gives the identity d^T B d = ||(I-Pbar)d||^2 - (1/4)||(P_1-P_0)d||^2 and the criterion ||(P_1-P_0)(I-Pbar)^{-1}||_2 <= 2 at the AVERAGE profile only; nothing there bounds the 2^{|C|} individual resolvents (I-Q_alpha)^{-1}, and the passage from the average to every selection --- via A-c = (A^2-c^2)/(A+c) with A+c <= 3 sqrt k ||d|| from substochasticity --- is the new step, and it is what converts a spectral condition into a probabilistic one.
results.argument: Write Pbar = (P_0+P_1)/2, Delta = (P_1-P_0)/2, Rbar = I-Pbar. Then d^T B d = (R_0 d).(R_1 d) = ||Rbar d||^2 - ||Delta d||^2 (rem:handicap-base's identity). Put A = ||Rbar d||, c = ||Delta d||; the hypothesis gives A^2-c^2 >= lambda||d||^2 > 0, so A > c. Every selection matrix is Q_alpha = Pbar + S Delta with S = diag(+-1) orthogonal, so ||(I-Q_alpha)d|| = ||Rbar d - S Delta d|| >= A - c = (A^2-c^2)/(A+c) >= lambda||d||^2/(A+c). Each P_a is substochastic, so ||P_a||_inf <= 1, ||P_a||_1 <= k, ||P_a||_2 <= sqrt k; hence A <= (1+sqrt k)||d||, c <= sqrt k ||d||, A+c <= 3 sqrt k ||d||. Invertibility of I-Q_alpha and nonnegativity of its inverse come from stopping (lem:survival-contract, Neumann series), and ||M||_inf <= sqrt k ||M||_2 for k x k matrices gives the infinity-norm form; ||(I-Q_alpha)^{-1}||_inf is exactly the largest expected number of C-visits under alpha.
results.verification: Exact rational arithmetic throughout. (a) 380 random stopping games in R (n = 3..8, |C| <= 5, seed 12345): the minimum over all 2^{|C|} selections of sigma_min(I-Q_alpha)^2 was compared with lambda^2/(9k), where lambda was obtained by exact bisection on the PSD test of B - lambda I; worst ratio 9.00, i.e. the bound held with a factor-3 margin in the worst case, and kappa*lambda/(3k) <= 0.334 in the worst case. (b) 3294 FRESH random stopping games in R at larger sizes (n = 6..14, seed 90210): kappa computed both by policy iteration on h = 1 + S h and by brute force over all selections (they agreed on every game), and kappa*lambda <= 3k on every one. (c) On the paper's families: WD(4,2,6),(6,3,7),(8,4,8),(10,5,9) have kappa = 16,64,256,1024 against lambda_min(B) = 2^-6,2^-9,2^-12,2^-15; CC(1,2),(2,2),(3,2),(4,2) have kappa = 4,16,64,256 against lambda = 2^-3,2^-6,2^-9,2^-12; HZ(4), HZ(6) have kappa = 2 with lambda = 1/4. In every case kappa <= 3k/lambda, with the families' kappa ~ lambda^{-2/3}.

results.name: ht:thm-kappa --- bounded visit number is a polynomial class
results.statement: There is an algorithm which, given a stopping SSG G and a bound K, either reports kappa(G) > K or outputs val exactly, in time polynomial in N and K; it is sound for every K and complete when kappa(G) <= K. Consequently {G : kappa(G) <= N^{O(1)}} is a polynomial class. The two ingredients are: (i) the n-horizon max-visit vector h_n satisfies h_n <= kappa(G) 1 even over history-dependent behaviour of both players (so non-stationary play does not visit more); (ii) sigma_n := ||S^n 1||_inf <= kappa(G)/n, where (S y)_v = max_a (P_a y)_v, so the reduced Shapley operator T_C is a 1/2-contraction after ceil(2 kappa) applications.
results.why_not_implied: thm:escape-class needs an escape certificate (lambda,x), x >= 1, S x <= lambda x, for the survival operator on ALL of V, average vertices included, and its round count is O((a + log kappa)/log(1/lambda)); prop:hz proves that HZ(n) admits no such certificate with lambda <= 1-2^{1-n}, so that bound is superpolynomial there, while kappa(HZ(n)) = 2. The new class eliminates the average vertices by one linear solve first, so a slow all-average part (the very device HZ uses to spoil the escape certificate and inflate the denominator) costs nothing.
results.argument: Compute P_a, r_a by one exact linear solve on Vavg. T_C(y)_v = max_a (P_a y + r_a)_v at Vmax, min_a at Vmin; val|_C is its unique fixed point (lem:survival-contract) and |T_C y - T_C z| <= S|y-z| pointwise, so ||T_C^n y - T_C^n z||_inf <= sigma_n ||y-z||_inf. (i) h_0 = 0, h_n = 1 + S h_{n-1} is nondecreasing by monotonicity of S, so h_n <= 1 + S h_n = 1 + Q_alpha h_n for a greedy selection alpha; hence (I-Q_alpha) h_n <= 1 and, multiplying by the nonnegative (I-Q_alpha)^{-1}, h_n <= kappa 1. (ii) let beta_j be greedy at S^{j-1}1, so S^n 1 = Q_{beta_n}...Q_{beta_1}1; each partial product Q_{beta_n}...Q_{beta_{n-i+1}}1 >= S^n 1 pointwise (because 1 >= S^{n-i}1 and the matrices are nonnegative), and the sum of the partial products over i = 0..n-1 is the expected number of visits within n steps under the single behaviour (beta_n,...,beta_1), hence at most h_n <= kappa; so n sigma_n <= kappa. Then iterate y_{j+1} = T_C y_j from 0 for J = ceil(2K)(2a+3) steps, obtaining ||y_J - val|_C|| <= 2^{-(2a+3)}; every value has denominator dividing an integer D <= 2^a (lem:denominator-sharp) and 2^{-(2a+3)} < 1/(2D^2), so lem:round-recover returns the exact values by continued fractions. Finally verify T_C(yhat) = yhat: if it holds, yhat = val|_C by uniqueness, and one linear solve extends val off C; if it fails, report kappa > K. Bit sizes grow by at most size(P_a,r_a) per step, hence stay polynomial. NOTE: this proves the claim recorded as (v11) in the round-19 briefing's list of UNVERIFIED claims from earlier rounds ('bounded kappa gives a polynomial algorithm unconditionally'); it is here proved, with the constants, and with the non-stationary clause that (v11) did not state.
results.verification: Exact rational arithmetic. (a) 295 random stopping games (seed 2024) and 3294 fresh larger ones (seed 90210, n = 6..14, |C| <= 5): sigma_n * n <= kappa verified for n = 1..7 on each; the algorithm was run with J = (floor(2 kappa)+1)(2a+3) iterations, the recovered vector was checked to be an exact fixed point of T_C, and it was checked to equal the brute-force w*|_C on every game. (b) HZ(4) (N = 98, |C| = 16, a = 80, kappa = 2): 820 iterations, exact recovery, T_C(yhat) = yhat verified, values with denominators like 15360 recovered exactly; HZ(6) (N = 218, |C| = 36, a = 180, kappa = 2): 1820 iterations, same, 19.6 s. So the algorithm was run end to end on the paper's own witness for 'outside every named bound'.

results.name: ht:cor-rlambda --- the strongly convex slice of R is a polynomial class, and rem:handicap-base's question has no positive answer there
results.statement: For lambda > 0 put R_lambda := {G stopping : B >= lambda I}. Then kappa(G) <= 3|C|/lambda on R_lambda and val is computed exactly in time polynomial in N and 1/lambda; in particular R_{1/p(N)} is a polynomial class for every polynomial p, and it contains HZ(n) (lambda = 1/4), which prop:hz places outside all eight polynomial classes of the paper. So no member of R_{1/poly} is outside the tractable instances, and prop:hz's ad hoc reduced 1/2-contraction is the special case lambda = 1/4 of a contraction available on the whole slice, of rate 1/2 per ceil(6|C|/lambda) applications of the reduced operator. Contrapositively, any family in R whose visit number is superpolynomial must have lambda_min(B) <= 3|C|/kappa.
results.why_not_implied: prop:hz is one family: it observes that in HZ(n) EVERY first-passage row over C has mass exactly 1/2, reads a 1/2-contraction off that circulant structure, and concludes for HZ(n) alone; rem:handicap-base then asks for a member of R outside the tractable classes. A general member of R_lambda has row masses arbitrarily close to 1 (DR(r,L) and DE(r) below have mass 1-2^{-r}), so no row-mass contraction is available, and the reduction of the spectral condition to a visit bound (ht:lem-sigmin) plus the non-stationary and decay lemmas is exactly what prop:hz does not contain. The paper explicitly records R as 'NOT a proved polynomial class (no first-principles convex-QP method)'; this is a first-principles proof for the slice, and it uses no convex programming at all.
results.argument: Combine ht:lem-sigmin (kappa <= 3|C|/lambda) with ht:thm-kappa (K := 3|C|/lambda). Membership in R_lambda is decided by one exact PSD test on B - lambda I after one linear solve, so the class is recognisable in polynomial time; and the algorithm certifies its own output, so even the test may be skipped. HZ(n) in R_{1/4} is prop:hz. The contrapositive is the inequality read backwards. Additionally {kappa <= K} is FREEZING-CLOSED (def:freeze turns a vertex into a sink, so first passages stop earlier and kappa cannot increase), so thm:modulator applies to it and gives N^{O(mu)} for the freezing-modulator number mu into it.
results.verification: kappa and lambda_min(B) recomputed from the game files, exactly: HZ(4) (N=98) and HZ(6) (N=218) have kappa = 2 (policy iteration on the max-visit MDP, all 16 resp. 36 coordinates of h equal to 2) and lambda = 1/4, and the algorithm returns the exact value vector on both (certified fixed point). WD(e,j,m) at (4,2,6),(6,3,7),(8,4,8),(10,5,9): kappa = 16,64,256,1024, lambda_min = 2^-6,2^-9,2^-12,2^-15, so kappa*lambda = 1/4,1/8,1/16,1/32 <= 3|C| = 6; CC(L,2) at L = 1..4: kappa = 4,16,64,256 with lambda = 2^-3,2^-6,2^-9,2^-12. Both certified families therefore sit deep inside the near-singular part of R, exactly as the contrapositive requires; on 3294 fresh random members of R the inequality kappa <= 3|C|/lambda held with margin.

results.name: ht:prop-damping --- R is not closed under damping
results.statement: There is a stopping SSG DR(8,38) on N = 74 vertices (2 Max, 72 average) which lies in R with lambda_min(B) = 4^{-8}, and whose uniform damping G_rho (def:discount-path) at rho = 1 - 2^{-7} does NOT lie in R: the direction d = (1,15/16) has d^T B_rho d < 0. G_rho is an honest SSG on 1082 vertices, built by lem:gadget with a chain of 7 average vertices on every edge, and B computed from that built game agrees exactly with the algebraic rho-rows. A single edge suffices too: DE(4) (N = 20, in R with lambda_min = 4^{-4}) leaves R when the one edge v_2 -> c'_1 is damped by beta = 2^{-2} (N = 22 after the gadget). The mechanism is general: any game whose two actions at each controlled vertex have the SAME first-passage row over C has P_0 = P_1, hence B = R^T R >= 0 and lies in R, and damping separates the rows.
results.why_not_implied: rem:handicap-base records that membership in R is a property of the presentation and that the SUBDIVISION of lem:splice carries 16 of 181 members out; the round-19 brief states that closure under Condon's damping (def:damping, def:discount-path) is open, and rem:signdef's damping-closure claim was struck for the different class of sign-definite games. Subdivision inserts Max vertices with equal successors and does not multiply any first-passage row; damping does, and the direction of the effect is not decidable from the subdivision result in three lines --- indeed 114000 random small games in R survived every rho tested, and the counterexample needs rho near 1 together with a delay chain of length ~1/(1-rho).
results.argument: (a) If P_0 = P_1 = P then B = R^T R with R = I - P, so B >= 0 and lambda_min = sigma_min(R)^2; in DR(r,L) both actions of v_1 enter chains with the same transition structure differing only in the sink they leak to, and both actions of v_2 enter the same chain, one of them through a delay e_j -> (e_{j+1}, e_{j+1}) which is lossless at rho = 1; so P_0 = P_1 = p*antidiag with p = 1-2^{-r} and lambda_min = (1-p)^2 = 4^{-r}. (b) Under killing rate 1-rho per step the chain contributes ell = sum_{j=1..r}(rho/2)^j, so p = q_0 = rho^2(1-(rho/2)^r)/(2-rho) and q_1 = rho^L q_0; with R_a = [[1,-p],[-q_a,1]], B_rho = [[1+q_0q_1, -(2p+q_0+q_1)/2],[-(2p+q_0+q_1)/2, 1+p^2]], and 4 det B_rho = 4(1+q_0q_1)(1+p^2) - (2p+q_0+q_1)^2 < 0 exactly when the damping has separated the rows enough while p stays above ~0.894. Both conditions are met at r = 8, L = 38, rho = 127/128.
results.verification: Exact rational arithmetic, and every number recomputed FROM THE GAME by two independent row routines (dense Gaussian elimination over the average vertices, and a topological-order sparse pass), which agree. DR(8,38): stopping by the trap test; P_0 = P_1 = [[0,255/256],[255/256,0]]; B = [[130561/65536, -255/128],[-255/128, 130561/65536]], LDL^T positive definite, lambda_min = 1/65536. The built damped game (1082 vertices, stopping) gives B_rho with det = -3.752e-05 and d = (1,15/16) with d^T B_rho d = -9.174e-06 (exact fraction printed by the script), and equals the algebraic rho-computation entry for entry. Re-run on fresh larger parameters: DR(9,60) (N=100, damped 1472), DR(10,80) (N=124, damped 1832), DR(9,45) (N=85, damped 1247), DR(12,120) (N=172, damped 2552) --- all in R undamped, all out of R damped, built game = algebraic rows in every case. Single edge: DE(3),(4),(5) with beta = 2^{-m}, m = 0..4, tabulated; DE(4) with m = 2 is the smallest found; an exhaustive sweep over all stopping games on two non-sink vertices found no witness (the n = 3 sweep was cut short by the time budget). Negative search context: 114000 random stopping games in R (n <= 12, |C| <= 5) with 21 values of rho each produced no counterexample --- which is why the construction had to be engineered.

results.name: ht:prop-cutform + ht:cor-cutwidth --- the tangent cut is a complementarity pairing, and what one cut buys
results.statement: Write eps_v = +1 at Vmax, -1 at Vmin, u_{v,a}(z) = eps_v(z(v)-z(v^{(a)})) >= 0 on Q(G), so q = sum_v u_{v,0}u_{v,1}. Then for x,y in the affine hull of Q(G), grad q(x).(y-x) = sum_v [u_{v,0}(x)u_{v,1}(y) + u_{v,1}(x)u_{v,0}(y)] - 2q(x), so the tangent cut of rem:tangent-cut at x is exactly sum_v [u_{v,0}(x)u_{v,1}(y) + u_{v,1}(x)u_{v,0}(y)] <= q(x), an inequality between sums of NONNEGATIVE products. Consequently, if x is the lexicographic maximiser of u_{v,i} over the current polytope P with M(v,i) := max_P u_{v,i} > 0, then the polytope P' after that one cut satisfies max_{P'} u_{v,ibar} <= q(x)/M(v,i) <= (sum_w min_a M(w,a))/M(v,i); with Phi(P) := max_w min_a M(w,a) and nu(P) := min_v max_a M(v,a), one round of M7 gives Phi(P') <= |C| Phi(P)/nu(P), and M7 is silent at v only if max_a M(v,a) > 0.
results.why_not_implied: rem:tangent-cut defines the cut through Taylor's formula on the affine hull, proves it sound on R, and records three decisions (WD at round one, BC(2,s) at round one or two, vertex 4 of the seven-vertex game at round one) together with 'no family designed against the cut exists yet'. It contains no algebraic normal form for the cut and no quantitative statement about what a cut removes; the bound max u_{v,ibar} <= q(x)/M(v,i) --- which is what a stalling family must defeat, and which says the invariant to preserve is q ~ nu*Phi at the cut points --- is not derivable from that remark in three lines.
results.argument: u_{v,a} is affine, so grad u_{v,a}(x).(y-x) = u_{v,a}(y) - u_{v,a}(x); the product rule on q = sum_v u_{v,0}u_{v,1} gives the first display, and grad q(x).(y-x) <= -q(x) rearranges to the second. Nonnegativity of every u_{v,a} on Q(G) is def:transport's defining inequality; dropping all terms of the pairing but u_{v,i}(x)u_{v,ibar}(y) = M(v,i) u_{v,ibar}(y) gives the bound. For the second inequality, q(x) = sum_w u_{w,0}(x)u_{w,1}(x) <= sum_w min_a M(w,a) * max_a M(w,a) <= sum_w min_a M(w,a) since every u <= 1 on Q(G). If max_a M(v,a) = 0 then u_{v,0} = u_{v,1} = 0 identically on P and reading (i) of rem:own-successor fires at v.
results.verification: Exact rational arithmetic, on random stopping games in R (seed 77, n = 3..7): for every controlled vertex, every action and every lexicographic optimum x with q(x) > 0, the identity grad q(x).(y-x) = (pairing) - 2q(x) and the equivalence (cut satisfied at y) <=> (pairing <= q(x)) were checked at 8085 point pairs (y ranging over vertices of the Z-seeded transport polytope maximising random integer objectives), and the consequence max_{P'} u_{v,ibar} * M(v,i) <= q(x) was checked by solving the LP over the polytope with that single cut adjoined --- it held at every one of those optima.

results.name: ht:prop-tworounds --- M7 is not a one-round mechanism
results.statement: On the stopping SSG W_10 with Vmax = {0,2,3}, Vmin empty, the other non-sinks average, t0 = 8, t1 = 9, and 0 -> (5,5), 1 -> (2,3), 2 -> (6,1), 3 -> (0,0), 4 -> (t1,1), 5 -> (t0,t1), 6 -> (7,5), 7 -> (3,4) --- every vertex reachable from the start 2, w* = (1/2, 8/15, 17/30, 1/2, 23/30, 1/2, 17/30, 19/30), vertex 2 the only value-distinguishing one, B over C = (0,2,3) equal to [[2,0,-1],[0,15/32,-5/16],[-1,-5/16,37/32]] positive definite (lambda_min ~ 0.2136, kappa = 4), so W_10 in R --- M7 with the paper's tie-break is silent at vertex 2 at rounds 0 and 1 and fires there by clause (ii) at round 2.
results.why_not_implied: rem:tangent-cut records only decisions AT round one (and round one or two for BC(2,s) 'according to the tie-break'); it exhibits no instance on which the cut is silent at round one, so 'M7 decides at round one on R' was consistent with everything in the paper --- and if it were a law then, by thm:decide-one-bit, all of R would be in P. The proposition rules that law out with an explicit game in R.
results.argument: Direct computation: the Z-seeded transport polytope of W_10 (def:transport with L = 1_{Z_1}, U = 1 - 1_{Z_0}), the six separators of the three readings of rem:own-successor at vertex 2, and the tangent cuts at the 8|C| lexicographic optima of (+-g_{v,i}, +-x(v)) with the tie-break of the paper's implementation (a first LP maximising the objective, a second maximising the secondary objective among the optima, the resulting basic solution). 17 cuts are added at round 0 and 17 more at round 1; every cut is checked to be valid at w*; every firing is checked against w* for soundness. The driver was validated by reproducing rem:tangent-cut's recorded behaviour: WD(4,2,6) and WD(6,3,7) silent at round 0 and decided at both Max vertices at round 1, and the seven-vertex game of rem:own-stall decided at vertices 1 and 3 at round 0 and at vertex 4 at round 1.
results.verification: Exact rational arithmetic (two-phase simplex with Bland's rule). W_10: stopping by the trap test, w* by brute force over all positional pairs, B and its LDL^T from the harmonic normal form, kappa = 4 by policy iteration and by brute force over the 8 selections. M7 run to K = 4 rounds: round 0 no reading fires at vertex 2, +17 cuts (49 rows), round 1 no reading fires, +17 cuts (66 rows), round 2 clause (ii) fires and names the optimal successor, which agrees with w*. Found by a random search over stopping games in R with a value-distinguishing vertex at which round 0 is silent; the search examined a few hundred such games within its time budget and produced this one instance with two rounds and none with three.

restatements.label: rem:handicap-base
restatements.note: The identity d^T B d = ||(I-Pbar)d||^2 - (1/4)||(P_1-P_0)d||^2, used as the first line of ht:lem-sigmin, is the paper's; only the passage from it to every selection is new.

restatements.label: rem:handicap-base
restatements.note: 'P_0 = P_1 implies B = R^T R >= 0, hence the game is in R' (the seed of the DR/DE construction) follows from the definition of B in three lines; it is stated inside ht:prop-damping only as a step, not claimed as a result.

restatements.label: thm:transport-objective
restatements.note: q >= 0 on Q(G) with unique zero w*, used to see that q(x) > 0 at every cut point other than w*, is the paper's.

gap: Three, stated exactly. (1) DELIVERABLE (A) IS NOT ACHIEVED: no family in R is exhibited on which M7 --- the Z-seeded transport polytope, the three readings of rem:own-successor and the tangent cuts at the 8|C| lexicographic optima --- is silent at a value-distinguishing vertex for superpolynomially many rounds; the missing statement is 'there is a family G_n of stopping SSGs in R, with N = poly(n) and a value-distinguishing controlled vertex v_n, such that M7 with the tie-break of scripts/round18-verify/hz_wedge.py is silent at v_n for at least 2^{Omega(n^c)} rounds'. What ht:cor-cutwidth adds is the invariant such a family must maintain (q at the cut points as large as nu*Phi round after round), and ht:cor-rlambda adds the necessary condition lambda_min(B) <= 3|C|/kappa. (2) R ITSELF (lambda = 0 allowed, and in particular the boundary attained by prop:handicap-singular) IS NOT SHOWN TO BE A POLYNOMIAL CLASS: the missing statement is 'there is an algorithm solving every stopping SSG with B >= 0 in time polynomial in N alone', which is the first-principles convex-quadratic-programming question rem:handicap-base already poses; my bound degrades to nothing as lambda -> 0. (3) THE STOPPING TRANSFORMATION IS NOT SETTLED: ht:prop-damping refutes closure of R under def:discount-path for SOME rho, but thm:stopping-transform uses the specific rho = 1 - 2^{-m} with m = ceil(2.5a + log N) + 3, and the DR construction needs a delay chain of length ~1/(1-rho) = 2^m, which would inflate a and hence m; the missing statement is 'there is a stopping SSG G in R whose damping at beta = 2^{-m} with m = ceil(2.5 a(G) + log N(G)) + 3 is not in R'.
next_steps: 1. The negative side now has a target with a proved necessary condition: a family designed against M7 must sit in R with lambda_min(B) = 2^{-omega(log N)} (else ht:cor-rlambda solves it and, more to the point, the polytope collapses), and by ht:cor-cutwidth it must keep q at the cut points comparable to nu*Phi. The natural next construction is |C| = Theta(N) --- at |C| = 2 the transport polytope is a plane polygon (lem:transport-dim) and Kelley on a plane polygon is short --- with B near-singular along one direction, i.e. a near-kernel direction of B carrying the value gap. 2. Ask whether the visit number is itself a REFORMULATION: is 'kappa(G) <= 2' target-equivalent under a size-preserving reduction? thm:top and thm:decide-one-bit suggest testing whether damping (which shrinks kappa but moves the threshold, cor:stopping-reduction) can push an arbitrary game into {kappa <= poly} at polynomial cost --- ht:prop-damping shows damping is not innocuous on the handicap, but the visit number is monotone under it, and the exact trade-off between kappa and the threshold shift is the question. 3. Close gap (2): either a first-principles polynomial method for min q over Q(G) with B >= 0 singular, or a proof that the boundary of R contains an instance outside {kappa <= poly} (prop:handicap-singular's 8-vertex game has a one-point seeded polytope, so a larger boundary instance is needed). 4. Settle gap (3) by computing d B_rho/d rho at rho = 1 for a game whose B is nearly singular: the perturbation is O((1-rho) * chain lengths) against a margin lambda_min, so a boundary instance of R with long chains is the place to look. 5. The exhaustive minimality sweep for the single-edge damping counterexample was cut off at three non-sink vertices; finishing it would give the smallest instance."

% Round-19 route: the handicap-zero class against its own cut.  Paste-ready; labels prefixed ht:.
% Full text is also in /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/c506180a-e393-4ffa-a18f-efc78c98397e/scratchpad/r19-handicap-tangent/ht.tex

\begin{definition}[Visit number]\label{ht:def-visits}
Let $G$ be a stopping SSG with controlled set $C$, $k:=|C|\ge1$, and let
$P_0,P_1$ be the first-passage matrices of the harmonic normal form over
$C$ (\Cref{rem:handicap-base}): $P_a(v,u)$ is the probability that the
walk started at $v^{(a)}$ meets $C$ first at $u$. For a \emph{selection}
$\alpha\in\{0,1\}^{C}$ write $Q_\alpha$ for the matrix whose $v$-th row is
$P_{\alpha(v)}(v,\cdot)$. Put
\[
  \kappa(G)\;:=\;\max_{\alpha\in\{0,1\}^{C}}\ \bigl\|(I-Q_\alpha)^{-1}\bigr\|_\infty ,
\]
the largest expected number of visits to $C$ under a positional pair,
counting the start. (Each $I-Q_\alpha$ is invertible because $G$ is
stopping, \Cref{lem:survival-contract}, and $(I-Q_\alpha)^{-1}=\sum_j Q_\alpha^j\ge0$.)
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[The handicap bounds every selection from below]\label{ht:lem-sigmin}
Let $G$ be stopping and $B\succeq\lambda I$ with $\lambda>0$ (so
$G\in\mathcal R_\lambda$). Then for every selection $\alpha$ and every
$d\in\mathbb R^{C}$,
\[
  \|(I-Q_\alpha)d\|_2\;\ge\;\frac{\lambda}{3\sqrt k}\,\|d\|_2 ,
\]
hence $\|(I-Q_\alpha)^{-1}\|_2\le3\sqrt k/\lambda$ and
$\kappa(G)\le3k/\lambda$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Write $\bar P:=\tfrac12(P_0+P_1)$, $\Delta:=\tfrac12(P_1-P_0)$,
$\bar R:=I-\bar P$. Then $R_0d=\bar Rd+\Delta d$ and $R_1d=\bar Rd-\Delta d$,
so $d^{\mathsf T}Bd=(R_0d)\cdot(R_1d)=\|\bar Rd\|^2-\|\Delta d\|^2$, which is the
identity of \Cref{rem:handicap-base}. Put $A:=\|\bar Rd\|$, $c:=\|\Delta d\|$;
the hypothesis gives $A^2-c^2\ge\lambda\|d\|^2>0$, so $A>c\ge0$.

Each $Q_\alpha$ is $\bar P+S\Delta$ with $S=\operatorname{diag}(\pm1)$
($+1$ where $\alpha(v)=1$), and $S$ is orthogonal, so
$\|(I-Q_\alpha)d\|=\|\bar Rd-S\Delta d\|\ge A-c$. Now
$A-c=(A^2-c^2)/(A+c)\ge\lambda\|d\|^2/(A+c)$. Every $P_a$ is substochastic,
so $\|P_a\|_\infty\le1$ and $\|P_a\|_1\le k$, whence
$\|P_a\|_2\le\sqrt{\|P_a\|_1\|P_a\|_\infty}\le\sqrt k$; therefore
$A\le(1+\sqrt k)\|d\|$ and $c\le\sqrt k\,\|d\|$, so $A+c\le(1+2\sqrt k)\|d\|\le3\sqrt k\|d\|$.
This gives the display. Consequently
$\|(I-Q_\alpha)^{-1}\|_2\le3\sqrt k/\lambda$, and for a $k\times k$ matrix
$\|M\|_\infty\le\sqrt k\|M\|_2$, so $\|(I-Q_\alpha)^{-1}\|_\infty\le3k/\lambda$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Non-stationary play does not visit more]\label{ht:lem-nonstat}
Let $G$ be stopping and let $h_n\in\mathbb R^{C}$ be defined by $h_0=0$ and
$h_{n}=\bbone+\mathcal S h_{n-1}$, where $(\mathcal S y)_v:=\max_a(P_ay)_v$;
$h_n(v)$ is the largest expected number of visits to $C$ among the first
$n$, from $v$, over all history-dependent behaviours of both players. Then
$h_n\le\kappa(G)\bbone$ for every $n$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
$\mathcal S$ is monotone, so $h_n$ is nondecreasing in $n$; hence
$h_n=\bbone+\mathcal Sh_{n-1}\le\bbone+\mathcal Sh_n=\bbone+Q_\alpha h_n$ for
a selection $\alpha$ attaining the maxima at $h_n$. Thus
$(I-Q_\alpha)h_n\le\bbone$, and multiplying by the nonnegative matrix
$(I-Q_\alpha)^{-1}$ gives $h_n\le(I-Q_\alpha)^{-1}\bbone\le\kappa(G)\bbone$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Survival decays at rate $\kappa$]\label{ht:lem-sigma}
With $\sigma_n:=\|\mathcal S^n\bbone\|_\infty$ (the largest probability of
$n$ further visits to $C$) one has $\sigma_n\le\kappa(G)/n$ for $n\ge1$;
in particular $\sigma_{n_0}\le\tfrac12$ for $n_0:=\lceil2\kappa(G)\rceil$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let $\beta_j$ be a selection attaining the maxima at $\mathcal S^{j-1}\bbone$,
so that $\mathcal S^{n}\bbone=Q_{\beta_n}Q_{\beta_{n-1}}\cdots Q_{\beta_1}\bbone$.
For $1\le i\le n$ the partial product satisfies
$Q_{\beta_n}\cdots Q_{\beta_{n-i+1}}\bbone\ge Q_{\beta_n}\cdots Q_{\beta_{n-i+1}}(\mathcal S^{n-i}\bbone)=\mathcal S^{n}\bbone$
pointwise, because $\bbone\ge\mathcal S^{n-i}\bbone$ and the matrices are
nonnegative. The left-hand sides are the probabilities of $i$ further visits
under the single non-stationary behaviour $(\beta_n,\dots,\beta_1)$, so their
sum over $i=0,\dots,n-1$ is at most $h_n\le\kappa(G)\bbone$
(\Cref{ht:lem-nonstat}). Hence $n\,\mathcal S^n\bbone\le\kappa(G)\bbone$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Bounded visit number is a polynomial class]\label{ht:thm-kappa}
There is an algorithm which, given a stopping SSG $G$ and a bound $K$, either
reports $\kappa(G)>K$ or outputs $\val$ exactly, in time polynomial in $N$ and
$K$. Consequently $\{G:\kappa(G)\le N^{O(1)}\}$ is a polynomial class.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Compute $P_a,r_a$ (the first-passage rows over $C$ and the weights of $t_1$)
by one exact linear solve on $\Vavg$; this is $O(a^3)$ rational operations on
numbers of polynomial bit size. Let $T_C(y)_v:=\max_a(P_ay+r_a)_v$ at
$v\in\Vmax$ and $\min_a$ at $v\in\Vmin$; by \Cref{lem:survival-contract}
$\val|_C$ is its unique fixed point, and
$|T_Cy-T_Cz|\le\mathcal S|y-z|$ pointwise, so
$\|T_C^ny-T_C^nz\|_\infty\le\sigma_n\|y-z\|_\infty$.
No test of the hypothesis is needed: set $n_0:=\lceil2K\rceil$ and iterate
$y_{j+1}:=T_Cy_j$ from $y_0:=0$ for $J:=n_0(2a+3)$ steps; by
\Cref{ht:lem-sigma}, $\|y_J-\val|_C\|_\infty\le2^{-(2a+3)}$. Every $\val(v)$
has denominator dividing an integer $D\le2^{a}$
(\Cref{lem:denominator-sharp}), and $2^{-(2a+3)}<1/(2D^2)$, so
\Cref{lem:round-recover} recovers each $\val(v)$ exactly from $y_J$ by
continued fractions. Finally check $T_C(\hat y)=\hat y$ on the recovered
vector $\hat y$: if it holds then $\hat y=\val|_C$ by uniqueness
(\Cref{lem:survival-contract}) and one further linear solve extends $\val$
off $C$; if it fails, report $\kappa(G)>K$. The procedure is therefore sound
whatever $K$ is, and complete when $\kappa(G)\le K$. The bit size of $y_j$
grows by at most the bit size of $(P_a,r_a)$ per step, so all numbers stay of
size $O(J\cdot\mathrm{poly}(N))$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[The strongly convex slice of $\mathcal R$ is polynomial]\label{ht:cor-rlambda}
For $\lambda>0$ let $\mathcal R_\lambda:=\{G\ \text{stopping}: B\succeq\lambda I\}$.
Then $\kappa(G)\le3|C|/\lambda$ on $\mathcal R_\lambda$, and $\val$ is computed
exactly in time polynomial in $N$ and $1/\lambda$. In particular
$\mathcal R_{1/p(N)}$ is a polynomial class for every polynomial $p$, and it
contains $\mathrm{HZ}(n)$ of \Cref{prop:hz} ($\lambda=\tfrac14$), which lies
outside all eight polynomial classes of this document. The question of
\Cref{rem:handicap-base} therefore has no positive answer inside the strongly
convex slice: no member of $\mathcal R_{1/\mathrm{poly}}$ is outside the
tractable instances, and the reduced contraction that \Cref{prop:hz} exhibits
by hand for $\mathrm{HZ}(n)$ is available on the whole slice, with rate
$\tfrac12$ per $\lceil6|C|/\lambda\rceil$ applications of the reduced operator.
Contrapositively, a family in $\mathcal R$ carrying a superpolynomial visit
number must have $\lambda_{\min}(B)\le3|C|/\kappa$, superpolynomially small:
as it is for $\mathrm{WD}(e,j,m)$ ($\lambda_{\min}=2^{-(e+j)}$, $\kappa=2^{2j}$)
and $CC(L,m)$ ($\lambda_{\min}=2^{-3L}$, $\kappa=4^{L}$).
\end{corollary}

\begin{remark}[The class is freezing-closed]\label{ht:rem-freeze}
Freezing a vertex at a payoff (\Cref{def:freeze}) turns it into a sink, so every
first passage that met it now stops there and $\kappa$ cannot increase:
$\{\kappa\le K\}$ is freezing-closed, and \Cref{thm:modulator} applies to it,
giving $N^{O(\mu)}$ for the freezing-modulator number $\mu$ into it.
($\mathcal R_\lambda$ itself is not obviously freezing-closed, $B$ being a
global object.)
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[$\mathcal R$ is not closed under damping]\label{ht:prop-damping}
For $r,L\ge1$ let $\mathrm{DR}(r,L)$ be the stopping SSG with
$\Vmax=\{v_1,v_2\}$, $\Vmin=\emptyset$, four chains
$a_j\to(v_2,a_{j+1})$, $a_r\to(v_2,t_0)$; $a'_j\to(v_2,a'_{j+1})$,
$a'_r\to(v_2,t_1)$; $c_j\to(v_1,c_{j+1})$, $c_r\to(v_1,t_0)$;
$c'_j\to(v_1,c'_{j+1})$, $c'_r\to(v_1,t_1)$; a delay
$e_j\to(e_{j+1},e_{j+1})$, $e_L\to(c'_1,c'_1)$; and
$v_1\to(a_1,a'_1)$, $v_2\to(c_1,e_1)$. Then $N=4r+L+4$, both Max vertices are
value-distinguishing, and
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item both actions of each $v_i$ have the \emph{same} first-passage row over
$C$ --- mass $p=1-2^{-r}$ on the other Max vertex --- so $P_0=P_1$,
$B=R_0^{\mathsf T}R_0\succ0$ with $\lambda_{\min}(B)=(1-p)^2=4^{-r}$, and
$\mathrm{DR}(r,L)\in\mathcal R$;
\item in $G_\rho$ (\Cref{def:discount-path}) the rows are
$p=q_0=\rho^2(1-(\rho/2)^r)/(2-\rho)$ and $q_1=\rho^{L}q_0$, so
\[
  B_\rho=\begin{psmallmatrix}1+q_0q_1&-\tfrac12(2p+q_0+q_1)\\
  -\tfrac12(2p+q_0+q_1)&1+p^{2}\end{psmallmatrix},\qquad
  4\det B_\rho=4(1+q_0q_1)(1+p^{2})-(2p+q_0+q_1)^{2},
\]
which is negative for $r=8$, $L=38$, $\rho=1-2^{-7}$ --- there $N=74$ and
$d=(1,\tfrac{15}{16})$ has $d^{\mathsf T}B_\rho d<0$.
\end{enumerate}
Hence $\mathcal R$ is not closed under \Cref{def:discount-path}, and not under
the damping gadget of \Cref{def:damping} either: the game $G_\rho$ above is an
honest SSG on $1082$ vertices, obtained from $\mathrm{DR}(8,38)$ by
\Cref{lem:gadget} with a chain of $7$ average vertices on every edge. A single
edge suffices as well: let $\mathrm{DE}(r)$ be the same construction with the
delay deleted, so $v_2\to(c_1,c'_1)$; it is in $\mathcal R$ with
$\lambda_{\min}=4^{-r}$, and damping the one edge $v_2\to c'_1$ by
$\beta=2^{-2}$ takes $\mathrm{DE}(4)$ ($N=20$) out of it ($N=22$ after the
gadget). No stopping game on two non-sink vertices does this for any single
edge and any $\beta=2^{-m}$, $m\le6$ (exhaustive).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(a) If $P_0=P_1=:P$ then $B=R^{\mathsf T}R\succeq0$ with $R=I-P$; here
$P=p\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, so
$\lambda_{\min}(B)=(1-p)^2$. The two actions of $v_1$ enter the chains $a$ and
$a'$, which have the same transition structure and differ only in the sink
they leak to, so their first-passage rows over $C=\{v_1,v_2\}$ agree; the two
actions of $v_2$ enter $c$ and, through the delay, $c'$, and the delay is
lossless at $\rho=1$ (both successors of $e_j$ are $e_{j+1}$), so those rows
agree too. The game is stopping because every cycle passes through a leaking
chain.
(b) With killing rate $1-\rho$ per step the chain $a$ contributes
$\ell(a_1)=\sum_{j=1}^{r}(\rho/2)^{j}$ and the row of $v_1$ is $\rho\ell(a_1)$,
which is the stated $p$; the delay multiplies by $\rho^{L}$. The displayed
$B_\rho$ is $\tfrac12(R_0^{\mathsf T}R_1+R_1^{\mathsf T}R_0)$ for
$R_a=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&-p\\-q_a&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. The
numerical claim was checked in exact arithmetic both from the algebraic rows
and from the built $1082$-vertex game, which agree.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The tangent cut is a complementarity pairing]\label{ht:prop-cutform}
Write $\varepsilon_v=+1$ at $\Vmax$, $-1$ at $\Vmin$ and
$u_{v,a}(z):=\varepsilon_v(z(v)-z(v^{(a)}))$, so that $u_{v,a}\ge0$ on $Q(G)$
and $q=\sum_{v}u_{v,0}u_{v,1}$. For $x,y$ in the affine hull of $Q(G)$,
\[
  \nabla q(x)\cdot(y-x)\;=\;\sum_{v\in C}\bigl[u_{v,0}(x)u_{v,1}(y)+u_{v,1}(x)u_{v,0}(y)\bigr]-2q(x),
\]
so the tangent cut of \Cref{rem:tangent-cut} at $x$ is exactly
\[
  \sum_{v\in C}\bigl[u_{v,0}(x)u_{v,1}(y)+u_{v,1}(x)u_{v,0}(y)\bigr]\;\le\;q(x),
\]
an inequality between sums of \emph{nonnegative} products on $Q(G)$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
$u_{v,a}$ is affine, so $\nabla u_{v,a}(x)\cdot(y-x)=u_{v,a}(y)-u_{v,a}(x)$;
the product rule on $q=\sum_v u_{v,0}u_{v,1}$ gives the first display, and the
cut $\nabla q(x)\cdot(y-x)\le-q(x)$ rearranges to the second. Nonnegativity of
each $u_{v,a}$ on $Q(G)$ is the defining inequality of \Cref{def:transport}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[What one cut buys]\label{ht:cor-cutwidth}
Let $P$ be the current polytope of \Cref{rem:tangent-cut}, let
$M(v,a):=\max_{y\in P}u_{v,a}(y)$, let $x$ be the lexicographic maximiser of
$u_{v,i}$ over $P$ --- one of the $8|C|$ cut points --- and suppose
$M(v,i)>0$. Then the polytope $P'$ after adjoining the cut at $x$ satisfies
\[
  \max_{y\in P'}u_{v,\bar\imath}(y)\;\le\;\frac{q(x)}{M(v,i)}\;\le\;
  \frac{1}{M(v,i)}\sum_{w\in C}\min_a M(w,a).
\]
Consequently, writing $\Phi(P):=\max_{w}\min_aM(w,a)$ and
$\nu(P):=\min_v\max_aM(v,a)$, one round of \textup{M7} gives
$\Phi(P')\le|C|\,\Phi(P)/\nu(P)$; and \textup{M7} is silent at $v$ at that
round only if $\max_aM(v,a)>0$. A family that keeps \textup{M7} silent must
therefore keep $q$ at the cut points as large as $\nu\Phi$ round after round.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
All the products in \Cref{ht:prop-cutform} are nonnegative on $Q(G)\supseteq P'$,
so dropping every term but $u_{v,i}(x)u_{v,\bar\imath}(y)=M(v,i)u_{v,\bar\imath}(y)$
gives the first inequality. For the second,
$q(x)=\sum_wu_{w,0}(x)u_{w,1}(x)\le\sum_w\min_aM(w,a)\cdot\max_aM(w,a)\le\sum_w\min_aM(w,a)$
because $u_{w,a}(x)\le M(w,a)\le1$. If $\max_aM(v,a)=0$ then
$u_{v,0}\equiv u_{v,1}\equiv0$ on $P$ and reading~(i) of
\Cref{rem:own-successor} fires at $v$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[\textup{M7} is not a one-round mechanism]\label{ht:prop-tworounds}
On the stopping SSG $W_{10}$ with $\Vmax=\{0,2,3\}$, $\Vmin=\emptyset$, the
other non-sinks average, $t_0=8$, $t_1=9$ and
$0\to(5,5)$, $1\to(2,3)$, $2\to(6,1)$, $3\to(0,0)$, $4\to(t_1,1)$,
$5\to(t_0,t_1)$, $6\to(7,5)$, $7\to(3,4)$ --- every vertex reachable from the
start $2$, $w^\ast=(\tfrac12,\tfrac8{15},\tfrac{17}{30},\tfrac12,
\tfrac{23}{30},\tfrac12,\tfrac{17}{30},\tfrac{19}{30})$, vertex $2$ the only
value-distinguishing one --- the matrix $B$ over $C=(0,2,3)$ is
$\left(\begin{smallmatrix}2&0&-1\\0&15/32&-5/16\\-1&-5/16&37/32\end{smallmatrix}\right)$,
positive definite ($\lambda_{\min}\approx0.2136$, $\kappa=4$), so
$W_{10}\in\mathcal R$; and \textup{M7} --- the $Z$-seeded transport polytope,
the three readings of \Cref{rem:own-successor}, and the tangent cuts at the
$8|C|$ lexicographic optima with the tie-break of
\texttt{scripts/round18-verify/hz\_wedge.py} --- is silent at vertex $2$ at
rounds $0$ and $1$ ($17$ cuts added at each) and fires there by clause~(ii) at
round $2$. So the round-one decisions recorded in \Cref{rem:tangent-cut} are
not a law: the tangent cut can be silent at round one on a game of
$\mathcal R$, and the same driver reproduces the recorded round-one decisions
on $\mathrm{WD}(4,2,6)$, $\mathrm{WD}(6,3,7)$ and on vertex $4$ of the
seven-vertex game of \Cref{rem:own-stall}.
\end{proposition}
prior_art: From memory, unchecked against sources. (1) That a $P$-matrix LCP with $M+M^{\mathsf T}\succeq0$ is solvable as a convex quadratic programme is standard (Cottle--Pang--Stone), and polynomial solvability of convex QP is Kozlov--Tarasov--Khachiyan; the paper already sets that route aside (rem:lcp, rem:handicap-base) and I import neither --- ht:thm-kappa uses no convex programming at all, only value iteration and Legendre's convergents. (2) The idea that the expected number of visits to the controlled vertices governs the convergence of value iteration on transient MDPs and stochastic games is classical (Veinott's transient MDPs; Puterman); Condon's own analyses use related quantities. What I do not recall in the literature is the passage from a spectral condition on $\mathrm{sym}(R_0^{\mathsf T}R_1)$ --- Gaertner--Ruest's 'handicap' of a $P$-matrix LCP --- to a uniform bound on the resolvents of all $2^{|C|}$ deterministic selections, which is ht:lem-sigmin; the handicap literature (de Klerk--E.-Nagy on exponential handicap; Vaeyaeranen--Kannan-type bounds) concerns interior-point iteration counts, not visit numbers. (3) The optimality of stationary policies for the total-reward criterion with nonnegative rewards (used implicitly in ht:lem-nonstat) is standard MDP theory (Blackwell; Puterman); I proved the one inequality I need from scratch, in two lines, rather than importing it. (4) Kelley's cutting-plane method and its lack of a polynomial rate are classical, as rem:tangent-cut already flags. (5) Within this project: ht:thm-kappa proves the claim recorded as (v11) among the round-19 briefing's UNVERIFIED claims from earlier rounds; that claim was stated without constants and without the non-stationary clause, and it is flagged here as an earlier round's observation now proved.
